intro.title: Explore the Oldest Historical Square in the Americas
intro.welcome: Welcome to Plaza de la Hispanidad or Spain, widely recognized as the central Plaza de la Hispanidad of Santo Domingo. Located in the heart of Santo Domingo, Distrito Nacional, Dominican Republic, this historic square serves as the primary hub for travelers visiting the region.
intro.description: Plaza de la Hispanidad (also known as Plaza de España) is located in the Zona Colonial, the historical core of Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. As an important part of the oldest surviving European settlement in the Americas, the square is adjacent to the Ozama River. It not only carries the profound history of the Age of Discovery but is now also the most vibrant cultural hub and public leisure space in Santo Domingo.

visitGuide.title: Amenities & Accessibility
items: ♿ Wheelchair Accessible: Highly friendly to wheelchair users and visitors with strollers. The overall area is flat and open, with complete accessibility facilities.
🐾 Dogs Allowed: This is an open area where pets are explicitly allowed, and local residents and tourists often bring their dogs here for walks and relaxation.
💡 Best Visit Time: Recommended to arrive in the evening (after 5:00 PM) to capture the soft light on ancient buildings and seamlessly transition to nighttime outdoor dining.

alsoKnownAs.title: Cultural Atmosphere
items: 🎭 Arts & Nightlife Hub: A major cultural activity center hosting outdoor art shows, live concerts, and other cultural celebrations year-round.
🍽️ Blend of History & Gastronomy: Cafes and restaurants with terraces along the edge of the square offer a perfect way to experience the local vibe.

route.title: Tour Route
route.overview: The ideal route to explore Plaza de la Hispanidad or Spain:
steps: Start at the main entrance at C. La Atarazana 2.
Walk along the paths and enjoy the park's landscapes and cultural elements.
Rest in the leisure areas and feel the local lifestyle.
Take photos of the park's beautiful scenery and historical architecture.
supplements: It's recommended to go during the day when the light is best for taking photos.
Pay attention to the park's opening hours and arrange your itinerary reasonably.
Please take care of the park environment and take your garbage with you.

sections.title: 🏛️ Alcázar de Colón
sections.content: Located on the east side of the square, built between 1510 and 1514. This was the residence of Diego Columbus, son of Christopher Columbus and then-governor. It is the oldest viceregal residence in the Americas, showcasing a blend of Gothic and Renaissance architectural styles.

sections.title: 🏰 Las Atarazanas
sections.content: Located on the west side of the square, this complex of brick and stone arches was the earliest customs house, armory, and shipyard in the Americas in the 16th century, now transformed into a famous dining and leisure district.

sections.title: 🎭 Vibrant Cultural Hub
sections.content: It is not just a static historical site, but a vibrant modern urban living room. It hosts various outdoor art exhibitions, live concerts, and other cultural celebrations throughout the year.

transport.title: Transportation
transport.airportDesc: From Las Américas International Airport (SDQ): About 28 km away. It is recommended to take a regular taxi or ride-hailing service (like Uber), traveling west on Autopista Las Américas and crossing the Ozama River bridge. The drive takes about 30-40 minutes.
transport.selfDriveDesc: As the Colonial Zone is a protected historical district with narrow one-way streets and no large public parking lots nearby, driving tourists are advised to park in compliant parking lots outside the zone and walk to the square.
transport.busDesc: Taking an Uber to the edge of the Colonial Zone and walking in is the most common and safest way to travel locally.
transport.intercityDesc: The entire Colonial Zone is very pedestrian-friendly. You can easily walk from the square to the Cathedral and other historical sites. The square is also highly wheelchair accessible.
transport.cyclingDesc: The square is paved with traditional cobblestones dating back centuries, but it is generally flat and open, suitable for a stroll.
transport.tipsDesc: For the best visual and cultural experience, it is recommended to arrive in the evening (after 5:00 PM), seamlessly connecting the illuminated night views and outdoor dining.

officialManagement.title: About Plaza de la Hispanidad or Spain
officialManagement.text: Plaza de la Hispanidad or Spain is a famous urban park in Santo Domingo, featuring beautiful landscapes and rich cultural value. It is directly managed and maintained by the Santo Domingo National District City Hall.

historyTimeline.title: Historical Timeline

items.title: Early 16th Century: Political and Trade Hub
items.plaque: Starting point of the Spanish Empire in the Americas
items.description: With the completion of the Alcázar de Colón and the Royal Shipyard, this place became the most important trade and political hub of the Spanish Empire in the Americas.

items.title: Late 20th Century: World Heritage
items.description: As part of the 'Colonial City of Santo Domingo', it was listed as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO.

items.title: 21st Century: Cultural and Leisure Center
items.description: After modernization and lighting improvements, it has become the most popular leisure, social, and dining square for tourists in the Dominican Republic.

historyTimeline.guideContent: Strolling from the ancient cobblestone roads of the 16th century to the outdoor restaurants of today, Plaza de la Hispanidad perfectly blends the weight of history with modern vitality. It is recommended that you arrive at dusk to personally experience this dialogue across five centuries of time and space.

nearby.title: Landmarks & Attractions Around Plaza de la Hispanidad
nearby.description: When visiting Plaza de la Hispanidad or Spain, visitors can easily explore surrounding historical landmarks and points of interest, including Alcázar de Colón and Las Atarazanas Reales, both part of Santo Domingo's UNESCO-listed Colonial City.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before visiting Plaza de la Hispanidad or Spain

items.name: Where is Plaza de la Hispanidad or Spain located?
items.text: Plaza de la Hispanidad or Spain is located at C. La Atarazana 2 in the Zona Colonial of Santo Domingo, Distrito Nacional, Dominican Republic (postal code 10212).

items.name: Is Plaza de la Hispanidad free to visit?
items.text: Yes, Plaza de la Hispanidad or Spain is a public open-air square and is free to visit all year round, 24 hours a day.

items.name: What is Plaza de la Hispanidad known for?
items.text: The square is the heart of the Colonial City of Santo Domingo, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It faces the historic Alcázar de Colón and the arcades of Las Atarazanas, blending 16th-century colonial history with vibrant outdoor dining and cultural events.

items.name: When is the best time to visit Plaza de la Hispanidad?
items.text: Late afternoon and evening, around 5:00 PM, is the best time to visit: the golden light falls on the colonial facades, and the square fills with terrace restaurants, live music and nightlife as darkness falls.

items.name: What other attractions are near Plaza de la Hispanidad?
items.text: The square is a short walk from Alcázar de Colón, the Atarazanas Reales arcades, the Catedral Primada de América, Parque Colón and the Ozama River esplanade, all inside Santo Domingo's pedestrian-friendly Zona Colonial.

items.name: Is Plaza de la Hispanidad accessible and pet friendly?
items.text: Yes. The square is flat, open and wheelchair accessible, and pets are allowed because it is a public open space.

items.name: Restrooms (WC)
items.text: Public restrooms are available in the square and the main public areas of the Colonial City; some are attended or require a small fee. Restrooms inside restaurants and cafés are usually reserved for customers, so it helps to locate public facilities before your visit.

items.name: Parking
items.text: The old town is a pedestrian-first district with narrow streets. Several paid public parking lots are located at the main entrances and around the Zona Colonial; it is best to park there and walk, take a taxi, or use city transit to reach the square.

items.name: Dining Options
items.text: Open-air terraces, cafés, dessert shops, and local food stalls line the square and the alleys of the Colonial City, offering Caribbean flavors, seafood, Latin grills, and Spanish-style dishes at every budget. We do not point to any specific business.

items.name: Lodging Options
items.text: The Colonial City and the old city wall host boutique hotels, traditional guesthouses, and vacation rentals, many set in restored colonial courtyard buildings. For a quieter and more convenient stay, consider options within walking distance of the square.

items.name: Shops & Services
items.text: Convenience stores, supermarkets, pharmacies, bank ATMs, and currency exchange points in nearby streets cover daily needs such as drinking water or a spare umbrella. Some small shops keep shorter hours on Sundays and holidays.

items.name: Fuel & EV Charging
items.text: Gas stations are common across Santo Domingo, most offering petrol and diesel, while public EV charging points concentrate in large shopping malls and along main avenues. Refuel or recharge before entering the old town to avoid maneuvering in narrow lanes.

story.title: History, Stories & Legends
story.lead: Behind a cobblestone lane, a coral-stone palace, and a row of arched arcades lie the memories of the first century of the New World. The accounts below follow early American chronicles and publicly available research, retold in plain language.

sections.heading: From Guacanagaríx to the First City of the Americas
sections.body: In December 1492 Columbus's fleet ran aground off the coast of the island of Hispaniola, in the lands of a Taíno chief named Guacanagaríx. Using timber from the wrecked ship, the crew built one of the earliest European outposts in the Americas - La Navidad - only to find it destroyed upon their return. In 1502 Governor Nicolás de Ovando moved the settlement to the western bank of the Ozama River and formally founded Santo Domingo, the first permanent European city in the New World. Its grid of streets, walls, churches, and plazas laid the foundation of urban civilization across the continent.

sections.heading: Diego Colón and the Oldest Palace of the Americas
sections.body: In 1509 Diego Colón, son of Christopher Columbus, arrived in Santo Domingo as governor together with his wife María de Toledo, a niece of King Ferdinand of Spain. Diego ordered a residence to be built on the high ground overlooking the Ozama River for his court; today we know this building as the Alcázar de Colón, the oldest surviving viceregal palace in the Americas, facing the square on its eastern side. To escape the Caribbean sun, María and the ladies of the court used to stroll along the city wall to watch the sea, and their path became known as Calle de las Damas - the first paved street recorded in the Americas.

sections.heading: Las Atarazanas Reales: Warehouse of the New World
sections.body: The arched stone arcades on the western side of the square belong to the Atarazanas Reales (Royal Shipyards), built around 1509 and regarded by scholars as one of the oldest surviving customs and royal warehouse complexes in the Americas. Gold, pearls, and precious cargo from the early Spanish conquest were inspected and stored here, while merchant fleets were fitted and supplied on the waterfront below. In 1586 the English privateer Sir Francis Drake seized Santo Domingo, demanded a huge ransom, and set parts of the city ablaze - giving rise to local tales of hidden treasure and ashes. Today, terraces and live music fill the arcades, yet the stone walls still tell of the commercial hub of the New World.

sections.heading: From Ruins to a Living Cultural Landmark
sections.body: From the 19th century onward the colonial district slowly declined and many buildings fell into ruin. A mid-20th-century restoration program revived the square and its surroundings and placed the entire district under heritage protection. In 1990 the Colonial City of Santo Domingo was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, turning this square into one of the most significant open-air classrooms on the colonial era of the Americas.

facts: Santo Domingo is often called the First City of the Americas, home to the New World's first cathedral, first hospital, first university, and first paved street.
The Alcázar de Colón was built from local coral stone with remarkably thick walls, strong enough to weather Caribbean hurricane seasons.
The square is also known as Plaza de España because it faces the heart of the old Spanish settlement.
In the evenings, the square hosts live Latin music as visitors and locals share the same stone steps under the open sky.
The Ozama River is Santo Domingo's mother river; the Fortaleza Ozama at its mouth is the oldest surviving European military fortress in the Americas.
